mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25 percentage points over the next month, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to turn negative due to tightened discount rates affecting future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25pp in the following month
failure_condition: In a tightening regime, the 20-day forward return is positive or flat, or the FEDFUNDS increase is not followed by a negative return within 20 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in PAYEMS (labor market additions) of at least 50,000 jobs over two consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days as hiring momentum boosts corporate earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >=50,000 over two consecutive months
failure_condition: No statistically significant positive return in 60 days after the two-month hiring surge, or the effect persists only in contractionary regimes.

mechanism_narrative: When GDPC1 (goods orders) grows faster than CPIAUCSL (inflation) over the prior quarter, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be positive as demand outpaces price pressures.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 quarterly growth rate > CPIAUCSL quarterly growth rate
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative when the condition holds, or the effect is not statistically significant in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) of more than 2% followed by a rebound of at least 1% in the next month predicts a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return as market anticipates softening supply chain activity.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls >2% in month t, then rises >=1% in month t+1
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is not significantly negative after the pattern, or the pattern does not occur in the data.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime where FEDFUNDS remains below 2% for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is expected to be positive as low rates encourage risk-on sentiment.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is not significantly positive when the condition holds, or the regime is not sustained.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in UNRATE (unemployment rate) below 4% followed by a sustained rise above 4.5% over the next 10 trading days predicts a negative S&P 500 10-day forward return as the labor market tightens and wage growth cools.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and then UNRATE > 4.5% within 10 days
failure_condition: The 10-day forward return is not negative when the trigger occurs, or the pattern is not observed in the data.

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (household spending) increases by at least 3% month-over-month for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be positive as consumer demand strengthens.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >=3% in month t and again in month t+1
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not significantly positive after the two consecutive months of spending growth.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both GDPC1 and RSAFS (goods orders and retail sales) exceeding their respective 5% monthly growth thresholds predicts a positive S&P 500 5-day forward return as dual demand channels strengthen.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > +5% and RSAFS > +5% in the same month
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is not positive when both proxies exceed thresholds, or the effect is not statistically significant in out-of-sample tests.
